narrative:
The model predicted that you have a 69.8% chance of failing the bar exam on your first attempt. Because the admissions process uses this prediction to assess risk, your application was rejected.

Three factors drove this outcome, ranked by importance. First, your LSAT score of 44 was the strongest influence, and it worked in your favor by pushing the prediction toward passing. Second, your first-year class ranking (decile 1) strongly pushed the model toward failure. While the average accepted student ranked around the 6th decile, you placed in the bottom decile, signaling early academic struggle. Third, your third-year ranking (decile 3) also pushed strongly toward failure. Again, this placed you at the very bottom of your class, compared to an average around the 6th decile among accepted students.

Although your solid LSAT performance pulled the prediction downward, the two weak academic rankings in law school carried more weight and ultimately led the model to forecast a high risk of bar exam failure.

You should focus on strengthening your academic record if possible, seek targeted bar exam preparation support, and consider reapplying once you have demonstrated clearer evidence of ability to succeed on the exam. Many students improve their outcomes through focused study after an initial setback.
